Booking.com and hotel software: the plumbing, direct booking, and AI agents

BKNG-hotel-connectivity-2026-10-12 · USD · series 2026-10-12T19:30:00Z · built 2026-10-13 12:23 UTC

The short version

Booking.com does not sit on top of hotels. It is wired into their software. Hotels push prices and rooms to Booking.com through a channel manager, and bookings come back down the same pipe into the property management system (PMS) that runs the front desk. More than 600 software vendors are certified to make that connection (S2). A hotel's own website is cheaper per booking on average, but not free: about 7% of booking value when the traffic is bought from Google and others, against the usual 15% to 25% online travel agency (OTA) commission (S6, S7). The worst-run quarter of hotels pays about as much going direct as they would to an OTA. AI assistants that simply read hotel websites cannot book reliably. The real bypass routes are direct connections to hotel software over MCP (Model Context Protocol), and they are now shipping: Apaleo and SiteMinder have them, and Google opened UCP for Lodging (S12, S13, S14). Each one reaches a single vendor's hotels and still lacks reviews, guarantees and customer service at Booking.com's scale. Booking.com has plugged itself into the same assistants first (S9, S10, S11).

How a Booking.com reservation actually moves

Booking.com's connection has two halves. Rates and availability (ARI: availability, rates and inventory) are pushed from the hotel side. Reservations are pulled by the channel manager, which acknowledges each one so none are lost (S1). Beyond that core, a connected vendor can also manage content, photos, guest reviews, guest messages, promotions and Payments by Booking.com onboarding (S1).

Channel managers include SiteMinder, D-EDGE, RateGain and Cloudbeds. PMS vendors include Oracle Opera, Mews, Apaleo, protel and Cloudbeds. Booking.com names its top 10% to 15% of vendors "Premier" each year (S2).

SystemWhat it doesWho uses itExample vendorsWhere it sits
Property management system (PMS)Runs the building: rooms, reservations, check-in, housekeeping, the guest's bill (S49)Every hotelOracle Opera (S49), Mews (S35), Cloudbeds (S36)End of every booking path
Channel managerSends one set of prices and rooms to every booking site and brings bookings back (S50)Mostly independentsSiteMinder (S50), D-EDGE (S51)Between the PMS and the OTAs
Central reservation system (CRS)One inventory and rate store for a whole chain, feeding the brand site, call centers, the GDS and OTAs (S52)Chains and hotel groupsSynXis by Aven, formerly Sabre, 35,000+ hotels (S52); Pegasus (S53)Above each hotel's PMS
Global distribution system (GDS)Network travel agents and corporate travel tools book through (S54)Chains; corporate and agency businessAmadeus, Sabre, Travelport (S54, S55, S56)Fed by the CRS
Booking engineThe "book now" checkout on the hotel's own website (S36, S50)Every hotel selling directCloudbeds, SiteMinder, D-EDGE, SynXis (S36, S50, S51, S52)Fed by the channel manager or CRS
Online travel agency (OTA)Marketplace where travelers search and book many hotels (S3)Sells for bothBooking.com, Expedia, AgodaFed by the channel manager or CRS

The overlap: chains run a CRS where an independent runs a channel manager (S52, S50), and many cloud PMS bundle the channel manager and booking engine. Cloudbeds One includes both (S36).

Direct booking on the hotel's own site

The direct channel has three advantages that an AI cannot copy for the hotel: it owns the guest's contact details, it can sell loyalty, and since the 2024 Digital Markets Act (DMA) designation Booking.com cannot stop a European hotel from pricing lower on its own site (S15). Google lets hotels list for free next to paid ads (S16).

The catch is demand. Being listed on an OTA also raises bookings on the hotel's own channels. In a Cornell test, listing on Expedia lifted non-OTA reservations by 7.5% to 26% (S17). That is the "billboard effect", and it cuts against any hotel that leaves Booking.com to save the commission.

Can AI assistants route around Booking.com?

Reading hotel websites is the weakest route. Live prices sit behind booking-engine scripts, Cloudflare now blocks AI crawlers by default on new sites (S18), and reading a page does not take a payment, issue a confirmation, or handle a cancellation or chargeback.

The direct route is real, but early:

IntegrationWhat it doesStatus
Apaleo MCP serverChatGPT, Claude and others can read and change reservations, rates and folios in Apaleo's PMS; about 230 actions; announced Sept 2025 (S12)Shipped
SiteMinder Channels Plus MCPLets a partner's AI list properties, create and confirm reservations across SiteMinder hotels (S13)Shipped, partner-only
Sabre MCP server and agentic APIsShop, book and service flights and hotels for travel agencies; Sept 2025 (S19)Announced, rolling out
Google UCP for LodgingHotels book inside AI Mode from their own CRS (central reservation system) and stay merchant of record (S14)Waitlist
Google AI Mode hotel bookingIn-chat booking in the U.S. with Booking.com, Expedia, Marriott, Hilton, IHG and others; Aug 2026 (S11)Shipped, U.S.
Expedia travel recommendations MCPSearch and recommendations, not bookings (S20)Shipped, read-only
Mews, Cloudbeds community MCP serversUnofficial open-source wrappers of the vendor APIs (S21)Hobby

Booking.com's answer is to be the default tool inside the assistants. It launched an AI trip planner on OpenAI's models in June 2023 (S24) and was an early partner on OpenAI's Operator agent in January 2025 (S26). Since then: an app in ChatGPT from launch day in October 2025 (S9), its own MCP server for approved partners (S10), and a launch-partner slot in Google's AI Mode booking (S11). In each, Booking.com supplies the inventory and the checkout.

The shift worth watching is who owns the front door. If assistants become the place trips start, Google and OpenAI gain bargaining power over every seller, Booking.com included. The PMS and channel-manager layer becomes more valuable whichever way the guest arrives, because every route ends there.

The hotel software market

The PMS market is small next to the companies selling rooms through it. Estimates for 2025 run from $4.57B (S27) to $6.04B (S30), with every firm projecting 7% to 10% a year growth (S27, S28, S29, S30, S31).

VendorWho uses itSize the vendor or a source printsShare

The Datanyze shares count companies where a vendor's software is detected, which favors small hotels with booking widgets. They are not revenue shares. No free source prints revenue share.

What it costs a hotel to plug into Booking.com

Booking.com charges nothing to connect. The hotel picks a certified connectivity provider, pays that vendor, and Booking.com maps the rooms (S37). The bill is the software:

ItemPublished priceSource
Cloudbeds One (PMS, channel manager, booking engine, payments)$11 per room a month, minimum $220S36
Cloudbeds setup$10 per room onboarding (min. $200) + $10 per room data import (min. $200); website setup $500S36
SiteMinder channel managerFrom €75 a month for a 5-room hotel; with booking engine and website, from €105; rises with roomsS38
Standalone booking enginesRoughly $60 to $300 a month, or a few percent per bookingS38, S6
MewsNo public price; about €300 a month floor reportedS39
Oracle Opera CloudNo public price. Partners connect through Oracle's paid, metered API platformS40
Booking.com connection$0 from Booking.comS37

Worked example (calculated; assumed $150 rate, 70% occupancy, one-third of rooms via OTAs — illustrative inputs): a 30-room independent on Cloudbeds One pays 30 × $11 = $330 a month, or $3,960 a year, plus $600 one-time setup. At a $150 average rate and 70% occupancy, that hotel sells about $1.15M of rooms a year, so the software is about 0.3% of revenue. One year of 15% commission on just a third of those rooms is about $57,000.

So far AI has moved the planning, not the payment. The new fee lines (metasearch per-booking tiers, AI-visibility marketing) land on the direct channel, while Booking's take stays about flat.

Watch list

  • Room nights growing slower than the hotel industry for several quarters, with no travel shock to explain it.
  • Marketing / revenue rising again while room nights slow: paying more for the same guest.
  • A large PMS or channel manager (Oracle, Mews, Cloudbeds, SiteMinder) shipping hotel booking inside ChatGPT or Gemini with payment, not just search.
  • Google UCP for Lodging opening to independent hotels through channel managers.
  • Booking.com losing a launch-partner slot in a major assistant, or a chain pulling inventory from Booking.com.

Open gaps

  • Booking does not print the share of room nights from independent hotels. Management says "the vast majority" (S5).
  • Booking prints app share, not a direct-traffic percentage.
  • Booking discloses only "less than 1%" of room nights from AI channels; no exact figure.
  • No free source prints PMS market share by revenue (IDC is paywalled). Apaleo and protel print no property counts.
  • Oracle Opera, protel, Shiji, SiteMinder Groups, IDeaS, Duetto and Mews print no prices.
  • Google AI Mode and ChatGPT publish no hotel booking fee.
  • Booking.com does not publish its average commission; the 15.8% to 17.5% figure is an industry estimate with no stated method.
  • Marriott says Bonvoy members booked about 68% of its room nights worldwide in 2025 (S22). Hilton does not print a comparable share.
